title: Global Markets Face Pressure as Borrowing Costs Reach New Highs
subtitle: Rising inflation and massive tech spending are changing how governments borrow money around the world.

summary.en: Global bond markets are seeing a major sell-off, causing borrowing costs for governments to reach levels not seen in decades. Tensions between the US and Iran have pushed up oil prices, fueling fears of higher inflation and interest rates. Meanwhile, large technology companies are borrowing massive amounts of money to fund artificial intelligence projects, creating new competition for capital. In the UK, Prime Minister Andy Burnham faces difficult choices ahead of his first budget as these rising costs limit his government's spending power. Experts suggest that these market pressures may force governments to make tough decisions regarding public spending and economic policy.
summary.zh: 全球債券市場正出現大規模拋售，導致各國政府的借貸成本達到數十年來未見的水準。美國與伊朗之間的緊張局勢推高了油價，加劇了對高通膨與高利率的擔憂。與此同時，大型科技公司為資助人工智慧專案而借入巨額資金，對資本市場造成了新的競爭。在英國，伯納姆首相在首份預算案前正面臨艱難抉擇，因為這些不斷上升的成本限制了政府的支出能力。專家認為，這些市場壓力可能會迫使各國政府在公共支出與經濟政策上做出艱難的決定。

paragraphs.en: Governments around the world are currently facing a difficult challenge as the cost of borrowing money reaches its highest level in decades. This situation, often described as a "bond market sell-off," occurs when investors sell their government bonds—loans made to a country—causing the interest rates, or "yields," on those loans to rise. According to BBC Business, this trend is creating significant pressure for world leaders who must now pay much more to borrow the cash they need to run their countries.
paragraphs.zh: 全球各國政府目前正面臨一項艱鉅的挑戰，因為借貸成本已達到數十年來的最高水準。這種情況通常被稱為「債券市場拋售」，發生在投資人賣出政府債券（即借給國家的貸款）時，導致這些貸款的利率（或稱「殖利率」）上升。根據英國廣播公司（BBC）商業新聞報導，這種趨勢正對各國領袖造成巨大壓力，因為他們現在必須支付高出許多的利息，才能借到維持國家運作所需的資金。

paragraphs.en: There are several reasons for this global shift. A major factor is the ongoing conflict between the US and Iran. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz and renewed fighting have pushed up the price of oil. When energy prices rise, inflation—the general increase in the price of goods and services—usually follows. This leads investors to expect that central banks will keep interest rates high to control prices, making government debt more expensive to manage.
paragraphs.zh: 造成這種全球性轉變的原因有幾個。一個主要因素是美國與伊朗之間持續的衝突。荷莫茲海峽的封鎖以及戰火重燃推高了油價。當能源價格上漲時，通常會隨之引發通貨膨脹，即商品與服務價格的普遍上漲。這導致投資人預期中央銀行將維持高利率以抑制物價，使得政府債務的管理成本變得更加昂貴。

paragraphs.en: Beyond geopolitical tensions, there is a new force changing the market: the massive investment in artificial intelligence (AI). Big tech companies like Google, Amazon, and Meta are borrowing hundreds of billions of dollars to build data centers. BBC Business reports that these companies have issued over $219 billion in debt this year, a huge increase from previous years. This surge in private borrowing creates more competition for money, which pushes up the price that governments must pay to attract investors.
paragraphs.zh: 除了地緣政治緊張局勢外，還有一股新力量正在改變市場：對人工智慧（AI）的大規模投資。像 Google、亞馬遜（Amazon）與 Meta 等大型科技公司正借入數千億美元來興建資料中心。BBC 商業新聞報導指出，這些公司今年已發行超過 2190 億美元的債務，較往年大幅增加。這種私人借貸的激增造成了資金競爭加劇，進而推高了政府為了吸引投資人所必須支付的成本。

paragraphs.en: In the United Kingdom, these global trends are hitting home just as Prime Minister Andy Burnham prepares for his first budget. The yield on 10-year UK government bonds, known as "gilts," recently jumped to nearly 5.3%, the highest level since 2008. The Guardian reports that these rising costs have significantly reduced the "headroom" the government has to spend money. This means the Chancellor, John Healey, has less money available for public services than he previously expected, forcing him to choose between raising taxes or cutting spending.
paragraphs.zh: 在英國，這些全球趨勢正對國內造成衝擊，而首相安迪·伯納姆（Andy Burnham）正準備提出他上任後的首份預算案。英國 10 年期政府公債（俗稱「金邊債券」）的殖利率近期飆升至近 5.3%，創下 2008 年以來的最高水準。《衛報》（The Guardian）報導稱，這些不斷上升的成本已大幅壓縮了政府的財政空間。這意味著財政大臣約翰·希利（John Healey）可用於公共服務的資金比預期來得少，迫使他必須在增稅或削減支出之間做出選擇。

paragraphs.en: Prime Minister Burnham has stated that his government’s foundation will be "fiscal responsibility," meaning they will aim to manage money carefully. However, he faces strong criticism from opposition leaders like Kemi Badenoch, who argue that his plans for economic growth are incorrect. The pressure is not limited to the UK; Japan is also dealing with high debt burdens and rising yields, while US markets have been rattled by attempts from the government to interfere in financial markets to lower interest rates.
paragraphs.zh: 伯納姆首相表示，其政府的基礎將是「財政責任」，意即他們將致力於謹慎管理資金。然而，他面臨來自反對黨領袖凱米·巴德諾赫（Kemi Badenoch）等人的強烈批評，後者認為他的經濟成長計畫並不正確。這種壓力不僅限於英國；日本也正處理沉重的債務負擔與不斷上升的殖利率，而美國市場則因政府試圖干預金融市場以降低利率的舉措而感到不安。

paragraphs.en: Experts are divided on the most important cause of this instability. Some, like economist Mohamed el-Erian, believe the massive borrowing by tech companies for AI is the biggest new factor. Others, such as Lord Jim O'Neill, point to the uncertainty surrounding US government policy. Lord O'Neill told BBC News that the current market pressure might eventually force political leaders to address difficult issues they have avoided for years, such as welfare spending and pension systems.
paragraphs.zh: 專家對於造成這種不穩定局勢的最重要原因看法分歧。有些人，如經濟學家穆罕默德·埃爾-埃里安（Mohamed el-Erian），認為科技公司為人工智慧進行的大規模借貸是最大的新因素。其他人，例如吉姆·歐尼爾勳爵（Lord Jim O'Neill），則指出美國政府政策的不確定性。歐尼爾勳爵告訴 BBC 新聞，目前的市場壓力最終可能會迫使政治領袖去處理他們多年來一直迴避的棘手問題，例如福利支出與退休金制度。

paragraphs.en: For the average person, these high borrowing costs are not just a matter for government officials. When government borrowing costs rise, it can lead to higher interest rates for businesses and families, making it more expensive to take out loans or mortgages. This creates a challenging environment for the economy as a whole.
paragraphs.zh: 對於一般民眾而言，這些高昂的借貸成本不僅僅是政府官員的事。當政府借貸成本上升時，可能會導致企業與家庭的利率隨之提高，使得申請貸款或房貸變得更加昂貴。這對整體經濟而言，創造了一個充滿挑戰的環境。

paragraphs.en: As the October budget approaches, the UK government is in a difficult position. The combination of high inflation, global conflict, and intense competition for money from tech giants has created a "brutal market equation," as described by BBC Business. If a country wants to borrow more money without a clear and credible plan, investors will demand higher interest rates. For Prime Minister Burnham and his team, the task ahead is to prove to the markets that they can manage the nation's finances while still delivering the changes they promised to the public. Whether they can balance these competing needs remains the most important question for the coming months.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著 10 月預算案的臨近，英國政府處於艱難的境地。正如 BBC 商業新聞所描述，高通膨、全球衝突以及科技巨頭對資金的激烈競爭，共同構成了一個「殘酷的市場等式」。如果一個國家想要在沒有明確且可信計畫的情況下借入更多資金，投資人將會要求更高的利率。對於伯納姆首相及其團隊而言，眼前的任務是向市場證明，他們既能管理國家財政，又能兌現對公眾承諾的改革。他們能否平衡這些相互衝突的需求，仍是未來幾個月最重要的問題。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To become clearly felt or realized, often in a painful or serious way.
keyTerms.definitionZh: （問題或情況）變得真實且令人難受，產生直接影響。
keyTerms.noteZh: 這是一個慣用語，字面上容易誤解為「打中家裡」。文中：In the United Kingdom, these global trends are hitting home just as Prime Minister Andy Burnham prepares for his first budget.

keyTerms.definitionEn: The amount of freedom or space available to act or spend within a set limit.
keyTerms.noteZh: 原意指車內或門框的高度，這裡指財政上的預算空間。文中：The Guardian reports that these rising costs have significantly reduced the "headroom" the government has to spend money.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To make someone or something feel nervous, worried, or unstable.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 使……感到不安、心慌或動搖。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（撥浪鼓或金屬碰撞聲），這裡作動詞表示市場受到驚嚇。文中：while US markets have been rattled by attempts from the government to interfere in financial markets to lower interest rates.

quiz.question: According to the article, what is the specific reason why tech companies' borrowing is affecting government debt costs?

options.A: They are directly lending money to the government at lower interest rates.
options.B: Their massive borrowing creates competition for available funds, driving up costs.
options.C: They are buying government bonds to secure their data center investments.
options.D: They are causing inflation by raising the prices of their tech services.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。文章第三段明確指出，科技巨頭為了建設數據中心而大規模借貸（超過2190億美元），這創造了對資金的激烈競爭，進而推高了政府為了吸引投資者所需支付的利息成本。選項 A 與文中提到的競爭關係相反；選項 C 文中未提及科技公司購買政府債券；選項 D 雖然提到科技公司，但文中將通膨歸因於能源價格上漲，而非科技服務價格。

quiz.question: Based on the text, what is the most likely consequence for a UK citizen if government bond yields remain high?

options.A: The government will be able to lower taxes to stimulate the economy.
options.B: The government will have more money to invest in public services.
options.C: It will become more expensive for the individual to secure a home loan.
options.D: The government will stop borrowing money entirely to balance the budget.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據第七段，當政府借貸成本上升時，這會導致企業和家庭的利率隨之提高，使得民眾申請貸款或房貸變得更加昂貴。選項 A 與 D 與文中提到的政府必須在加稅或削減支出之間做選擇的困境相矛盾；選項 B 錯誤，因為第四段提到高債券殖利率反而減少了政府用於公共服務的「預算空間（headroom）」。

quiz.question: In the fourth paragraph, what does the word 'headroom' mean in the context of the UK government's budget?

options.A: The physical height of the government office building.
options.B: The amount of money available for discretionary spending.
options.C: The total debt the government is allowed to owe.
options.D: The time remaining before the next general election.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。在此語境下，「headroom」並非指物理空間，而是指財政上的「餘裕」或「空間」，即政府在扣除必要支出後，還能有多少資金用於公共服務。選項 A 是字面意思的誤解；選項 C 指的是債務上限，與文中描述的預算彈性不同；選項 D 與選舉時間無關。文中提到因為成本上升，這種餘裕被顯著縮減，迫使政府必須做出艱難的選擇。

quiz.question: What is the central message of the article regarding the current global economic situation?

options.A: The UK government is solely responsible for the current rise in global interest rates.
options.B: Artificial intelligence is the only factor causing the instability in the bond market.
options.C: Governments are struggling to balance fiscal needs amidst complex global pressures and high borrowing costs.
options.D: Investors are no longer interested in buying government bonds because of the conflict in Iran.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章全面探討了全球政府面臨的共同挑戰，包括地緣政治（能源價格）、科技業借貸競爭以及國內財政壓力，並以英國為例說明政府如何在這些壓力下試圖維持財政責任。選項 A 過於狹隘，未涵蓋全球因素；選項 B 錯誤，因為文中提到多種因素（能源、地緣政治、科技借貸）；選項 D 不正確，投資者仍在市場中，只是要求更高的利率。
